business_request.question: Explain the registered NSK Smearing 7 example: how is its bearing identity linked to Smearing 5, what surface damage is reported and what cause is attributed? Does the rolling_element category establish the same damage or cause in the CWRU bearing?

draft.answer: The registered NSK example links Smearing 7 to Smearing 5: the convex rollers in Smearing 7 belong to the same spherical roller bearing shown in Smearing 5, and the manufacturer reports smearing of the rolling surfaces on those convex rollers, attributing that example to poor lubrication [EV-I01-002]. The source also gives general smearing context—surface damage from small seizures between bearing components due to oil-film rupture and/or sliding, with possible causes including high speed and light load, sudden acceleration/deceleration, improper lubricant, and water entry [EV-I01-002]. The caller-assigned rolling_element category does not establish the same damage or cause in the CWRU bearing: the source is a spherical roller bearing example, not a CWRU deep-groove ball bearing, and the rolling-element classification does not prove smearing or a lubrication cause [EV-I01-002]. The poor-lubrication spherical-roller-smearing scenario is an independently specified teaching assumption, not an observation or classifier inference, and no sample root cause, lubricant specification/quantity, or model-specific threshold is established [EV-I01-002].
